facts.content: Patient reports ongoing central chest pressure since gardening a few hours ago.
facts.source_text: CC: Ongoing central chest pressure since gardening a few hrs ago

facts.content: The chest pressure is described as feeling like someone sitting on the chest and is diffuse.
facts.source_text: Pressure “like someone sitting on chest,” diffuse;

facts.content: The chest pressure radiates to the left arm and shoulder.
The chest pressure is associated with shortness of breath, diaphoresis, and nausea.
The patient denies vomiting.
The chest pressure was persistent at the time of the call.
This is the first episode of this chest pain.
Onset of chest pain occurred while kneeling and was not during strenuous activity.
The patient feels the heart rate is faster now and attributes this to stress.
Patient has a history of hypertension.
Patient has no history of diabetes mellitus.
The patient reports cholesterol has never been checked.
Medications were not discussed during this encounter.
Patient has a mild, non–life-threatening allergic reaction to aspirin and has taken it before.
facts.source_text: Allergies: ASA — mild allergic rxn (non–life-threatening; has taken before)

facts.content: The patient's father died of myocardial infarction at approximately age 60.
The patient's mother has unspecified heart problems.
The patient smokes about 10 cigarettes per day for 15 years.
The patient drinks approximately 7 to 8 pints of beer per week.
The patient is described as overweight.
The patient lives alone.
The patient is a restaurant owner of a sushi establishment.
The patient has low baseline physical activity.
Patient has acute chest pain with high concern for acute coronary syndrome due to ongoing central pressure with left arm radiation, shortness of breath, diaphoresis, and nausea.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute chest pain — high concern for ACS given ongoing central pressure with L arm radiation, SOB, diaphoresis, nausea;

facts.content: The patient has cardiovascular risk factors including hypertension, smoking, family history of premature coronary artery disease, and being overweight.
facts.source_text: RFs: HTN, smoker, FHx of premature CAD, overweight

facts.content: Emergency medical services were activated and the clinician will remain on the line until their arrival.
facts.source_text: EMS activated; clinician to remain on line until arrival

facts.content: The patient is to wait near an open front door to facilitate EMS access.
facts.source_text: Pt to wait near open front door to facilitate access

facts.content: A handover will be given to EMS on arrival.
